title: SAGE Lifecycle State Machine Configuration
description: Defines lifecycle states and valid transitions for documents in a vault. The base state machine (active, completed, archived) is always present. Vaults may define additional states and transitions. See SAGE Architecture Reference Section 4.8.

states.description: All lifecycle states available in this vault, including the base set and any domain-specific additions.

value.description: Machine identifier for the lifecycle state.

description.description: Semantics of this state. For base states: active (in the system), completed (work done, no replacement), archived (long-term storage; includes documents superseded by newer versions).

is_terminal.description: Whether this state represents an end state from which no further transitions are expected under normal operation. Archived is terminal by default but reactivation is permitted as an exceptional case.

satisfies_dependency.description: Whether documents in this state satisfy inbound depends_on preconditions. Omitted or null defers to the engine default: active and completed satisfy, every other state does not. Set true to let a domain-specific state satisfy dependencies, or false to exclude a base state.

transitions.description: Valid state transitions. SAGE enforces transition validity; the orchestration layer determines when to trigger transitions.

from_state.description: Source state. Use '(new)' for the initial ingestion transition.

action.description: The action that triggers this transition. Base actions: ingest, supersede, complete, archive, reactivate.

semantics.description: What this transition means. Key distinction: supersede means a newer version exists (supersedes edge created); complete means work is done but no replacement was needed.

creates_edge.description: If this transition automatically creates a graph edge, the edge_type value. The supersede action creates a 'supersedes' edge from the new version to the old.

base_states_required.description: When true (the default), the configuration must declare the base states (active, completed, archived) and use each base action (ingest, supersede, complete, archive, reactivate) in at least one transition; a configuration missing any of them is rejected at load. Domain-specific states and transitions extend this base. Set false only for a configuration that replaces the base lifecycle entirely.
